## Introduction Brotli is a generic-purpose lossless compression algorithm that compresses data using a combination of a modern variant of the LZ77 algorithm, Huffman coding and 2nd order context modeling, with a compression ratio comparable to the best currently available general-purpose compression methods. It is similar in speed with deflate but offers more dense compression. The specification of the Brotli Compressed Data Format is defined in [RFC 7932](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7932). Brotli is open-sourced under the MIT License, see the LICENSE file. > **Please note:** brotli is a "stream" format; it does not contain > meta-information, like checksums or uncompressed data length. It is possible > to modify "raw" ranges of the compressed stream and the decoder will not > notice that. ## Command-Line Tool The `brotli` command-line tool can compress and decompress files. ### Basic Usage Compress a file: ``` brotli input.txt ``` Decompress a file: ``` brotli --decompress input.txt.br ``` Compress to stdout: ``` brotli --stdout input.txt > output.br ``` Decompress from stdin: ``` cat input.txt.br | brotli --decompress --stdout ``` ### Command Aliases - `brcat` is equivalent to `brotli --decompress --concatenated --stdout` - `unbrotli` is equivalent to `brotli --decompress` ### Common Options - `-#` or `--quality=#`: Set compression quality (0-11, default: 11) - `-d` or `--decompress`: Decompress mode - `-c` or `--stdout`: Write to stdout - `-f` or `--force`: Overwrite existing output files - `-k` or `--keep`: Keep input files (default behavior) - `--rm`: Remove input files after processing - `-t` or `--test`: Test compressed file integrity - `-v` or `--verbose`: Verbose output - `-h` or `--help`: Display help information - `-V` or `--version`: Display version information ### Operation Modes 1. **Compression mode** (default): Compress input files 2. **Decompression mode** (`--decompress`): Decompress input files 3. **Test mode** (`--test`): Verify integrity of compressed files ### Examples Compress with specific quality level: ``` brotli -q 9 input.txt ``` Decompress multiple files: ``` brotli -d file1.br file2.br file3.br ``` Compress and remove original: ``` brotli --rm input.txt ``` Test compressed file: ``` brotli --test file.br ``` For more detailed information, see the brotli(1) manual page. --- # Brotli

\f[B]zstd (1)\f[R].

\f[B]--rm\f[R] \f[I]option\f[R].

.IP \[bu] 2
default mode is compression;
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]--decompress\f[R] option activates decompression mode;

.PP
Every non-option argument is a \f[I]file\f[R] entry.
If no \f[I]files\f[R] are given or \f[I]file\f[R] is
\[lq]\f[B]-\f[R]\[rq], \f[B]brotli\f[R] reads from standard input.
All arguments after \[lq]\f[B]--\f[R]\[rq] are \f[I]file\f[R] entries.
.PP
Unless \f[B]--stdout\f[R] or \f[B]--output\f[R] is specified,
\f[I]files\f[R] are written to a new file whose name is derived from the
source \f[I]file\f[R] name:
.IP \[bu] 2
when compressing, a suffix is appended to the source filename to get the
target filename
.IP \[bu] 2
when decompressing, a suffix is removed from the source filename to get
the target filename
.PP
Default suffix is \f[B].br\f[R], but it could be specified with
\f[B]--suffix\f[R] option.
.PP
Conflicting or duplicate \f[I]options\f[R] are not allowed.
.SH OPTIONS
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-#\f[R]: compression level (0-9); bigger values cause denser, but
slower compression
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-c\f[R], \f[B]--stdout\f[R]: write on standard output
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-d\f[R], \f[B]--decompress\f[R]: decompress mode
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-f\f[R], \f[B]--force\f[R]: force output file overwrite
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-h\f[R], \f[B]--help\f[R]: display this help and exit
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-j\f[R], \f[B]--rm\f[R]: remove source file(s); \f[B]gzip
(1)\f[R]-like behaviour
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-k\f[R], \f[B]--keep\f[R]: keep source file(s); \f[B]zstd
(1)\f[R]-like behaviour
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-n\f[R], \f[B]--no-copy-stat\f[R]: do not copy source file(s)
attributes
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-o FILE\f[R], \f[B]--output=FILE\f[R] output file; valid only if
there is a single input entry
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-q NUM\f[R], \f[B]--quality=NUM\f[R]: compression level (0-11);
bigger values cause denser, but slower compression
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-t\f[R], \f[B]--test\f[R]: test file integrity mode
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-v\f[R], \f[B]--verbose\f[R]: increase output verbosity
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-w NUM\f[R], \f[B]--lgwin=NUM\f[R]: set LZ77 window size (0, 10-24)
(default: 24); window size is \f[B](pow(2, NUM) - 16)\f[R]; 0 lets
compressor decide over the optimal value; bigger windows size improve
density; decoder might require up to window size memory to operate
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-C B64\f[R], \f[B]--comment=B64\f[R]: set comment; argument is
base64-decoded first; when decoding: check stream comment; when
encoding: embed comment (fingerprint)
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-D FILE\f[R], \f[B]--dictionary=FILE\f[R]: use FILE as raw (LZ77)
dictionary; same dictionary MUST be used both for compression and
decompression
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-K\f[R], \f[B]--concatenated\f[R]: when decoding, allow
concatenated brotli streams as input
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-S SUF\f[R], \f[B]--suffix=SUF\f[R]: output file suffix (default:
\f[B].br\f[R])
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-V\f[R], \f[B]--version\f[R]: display version and exit
.IP \[bu] 2
\f[B]-Z\f[R], \f[B]--best\f[R]: use best compression level (default);
same as \[lq]\f[B]-q 11\f[R]\[rq]
.SH SEE ALSO
.PP
\f[B]brotli\f[R] file format is defined in RFC
7932 (https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7932.txt).
.PP

.PP

enc.BrotliEncoderMaxCompressedSize.restype = ctypes.c_size_t
enc.BrotliEncoderMaxCompressedSize.argtypes = [ctypes.c_size_t]

def compress(data, quality=11, lgwin=24):
    insize = len(data)
    maxsize = enc.BrotliEncoderMaxCompressedSize(insize)
    outbuf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(maxsize if maxsize>0 else 1024)
    outsize = ctypes.c_size_t(maxsize if maxsize>0 else 1024)
    # quality, lgwin, mode? mode 0 generic? BrotliEncoderCompress(quality, lgwin, mode, input_size, input, *encoded_size, encoded)
    # mode: 0 generic, 1 text, 2 font? Use 0?
    # Actually signature: int BrotliEncoderCompress(int quality, int lgwin, int mode, size_t input_size, const uint8_t* input_buffer, size_t* encoded_size, uint8_t* encoded_buffer)
    # Try mode 0
    ret = enc.BrotliEncoderCompress(quality, lgwin, 0, insize, data, ctypes.byref(outsize), outbuf)
    print(f"quality={quality} lgwin={lgwin} ret={ret} outsize={outsize.value}")
    return bytes(outbuf.raw[:outsize.value]) if ret==1 else None

import subprocess
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def exe_compress(data, extra_args=[]):
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+extra_args, input=data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd="/tmp")

    print(f"q={q} syslen={len(a) if a else 'fail'} exelen={len(b)} equal={a==b}")
    if a!=b:

# what content? Should be last file's compressed?

# need fresh for multi? stdout multi gave usage earlier

print(f"stdout multi rc={rc} usage={len(out)>1000} err={err!r}")

# Actually need to capture correctly

print(f"stdout file+stdin rc={p.returncode} usage={len(p.stdout)>1000} err={p.stderr!r} out_len={len(p.stdout)}")

import subprocess, os, shutil, re
EXE_ORIG="/workspace/executable"
EXE_NEW="/tmp/prog_test/executable"

def fresh(dir, files={"a.txt": b"hello world "*100, "b.txt": b"world hello "*50}):
    shutil.rmtree(dir, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(dir, exist_ok=True)
    for k,v in files.items():
        open(f"{dir}/{k}","wb").write(v)

def run_and_compare(args, stdin_data=b"", need_br=False):
    # need_br: if decompress/test, need to create .br first
    results=[]
    for exe, dir in [(EXE_ORIG,"/tmp/cmp_orig"), (EXE_NEW,"/tmp/cmp_new")]:
        fresh(dir)
        if need_br:
            # compress to create .br
            subprocess.run([exe,"a.txt","b.txt"], cwd=dir, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
            # remove originals as needed for test? For single file decompress, need to remove a.txt to allow output
            # For our tests, we'll remove a.txt for single, both for multi
            # Determine files in args
            file_args = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("-") and a not in [""]]
            if len(file_args)==1 and file_args[0].endswith(".br"):
                # single decompress: remove corresponding txt
                txt = file_args[0][:-3]
                try: os.unlink(f"{dir}/{txt}")
                except: pass
            elif len(file_args)>1:
                for f in ["a.txt","b.txt"]:
                    try: os.unlink(f"{dir}/{f}")
                    except: pass
        p=subprocess.run([exe]+args, input=stdin_data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=dir)
        err_norm=re.sub(rb" in [0-9]+\.[0-9]+ sec", b" in TIME sec", p.stderr)
        # collect file contents
        file_contents={}
        for f in sorted(os.listdir(dir)):
            try:
                file_contents[f]=open(f"{dir}/{f}","rb").read()
            except: pass
        results.append((p.returncode, p.stdout, err_norm, sorted(os.listdir(dir)), file_contents))
    (rc1,out1,err1,ls1,fc1),(rc2,out2,err2,ls2,fc2)=results
    ok = (rc1==rc2 and out1==out2 and err1==err2 and ls1==ls2 and fc1==fc2)
    status="PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status} {args} stdin_len={len(stdin_data)}")
    if not ok:
        print(f"  orig rc={rc1} out={out1[:60]!r} err={err1!r} ls={ls1}")
        print(f"  new  rc={rc2} out={out2[:60]!r} err={err2!r} ls={ls2}")
        if fc1!=fc2:
            for k in set(list(fc1.keys())+list(fc2.keys())):
                if fc1.get(k)!=fc2.get(k):
                    print(f"   file {k} differs {len(fc1.get(k,b''))} vs {len(fc2.get(k,b''))}")

# Test many
for q in [0,1,5,9,11]:
    run_and_compare(["--quality="+str(q),"a.txt"])
    run_and_compare(["--quality="+str(q)], stdin_data=b"hello world "*20)
for lg in [10,16,22,24,0]:
    run_and_compare([f"--lgwin={lg}","a.txt"])
    run_and_compare([f"--lgwin={lg}"], stdin_data=b"hello "*50)
for lw in [10,24,30,0]:
    run_and_compare([f"--large_window={lw}","a.txt"])

run_and_compare(["-9","a.txt"])
run_and_compare(["-Z","a.txt"])
run_and_compare(["-d","a.txt.br"], need_br=True)
run_and_compare(["-d","-c","a.txt.br"], need_br=True)
run_and_compare(["-t","a.txt.br"], need_br=True)
run_and_compare(["-t","a.txt.br","b.txt.br"], need_br=True)
run_and_compare(["-d","-K","combined.br"], need_br=False)  # need combined? skip for now
